### 1. Workspace Initialization

This R Markdown document prepares the data and figures for the Climate 
Change Vulnerability Assessment for Logan Pass Water Supplies at Glacier 
National Park.

```{r setup}
# --- 1. Global Knitr Options ---
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  eval    = TRUE
)

# --- 2. Load Data and Dependencies ---
# Load site-specific datasets for GLAC
load("data/park/GLAC/GLAC_data.RData")

# Source custom functions and libraries (loads tidyverse, sf, etc.)
source('setup.R')

# Additional packages used in downstream chunks (loaded here to avoid
# mid-document library() calls)
library(ggpubr)
library(GGally)
library(osmdata)
library(ggpattern)

# --- 3. Interactive Map Configuration ---
# Configure mapview defaults for standard Esri basemaps
mapviewOptions(
  fgb      = FALSE,
  georaster = FALSE,
  basemaps  = c("CartoDB.Positron", "Esri.WorldTopoMap", "Esri.WorldImagery")
)

# --- 4. Color Palettes ---
# Standard project palette
pal <- list(
  black     = "black",
  gold      = "#dca237",
  lightblue = "#6eb2e4",
  teal      = "#459a74",
  yellow    = "#eee461",
  darkblue  = "#3070ad",
  orange    = "#c66426",
  pink      = "#c07da5",
  lightpink = "#ECD8E4"
)

# NPS-specific branding palette
nps_pal <- list(
  blue      = "#85b6dc",
  red       = "#c5312a",
  grey      = "#a9a9a9",
  lightgrey = "#dcdcdc"
)

# Named CF color vector — used throughout all figures
plot_colors <- c(
  "Historical" = "#a9a9a9",
  "Hot Dry"    = "#c5312a",
  "Warm Wet"   = "#85b6dc"
)

# --- 5. Shared ggplot Helpers ---

# Convenience wrappers: apply the standard CF color scheme with one call
scale_fill_cf  <- function(...) scale_fill_manual("",  values = plot_colors, ...)
scale_color_cf <- function(...) scale_color_manual("", values = plot_colors, ...)

# Standard bottom-legend theme with a tight negative top margin
theme_legend_bottom <- theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.margin   = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)
)

# --- 6. Hydrological Constants & Timeframes ---
# Unit conversions: Cubic Feet <-> Gallons
gal_to_cf <- 0.1336805
cf_to_gal <- 1 / gal_to_cf

# Analysis windows used by every chunk (inclusive). The WBM is run from 1979,
# which is a spin-up year and is excluded from all statistics.
hist_yrs <- c(1980, 2012)   # Historical baseline period
fut_yrs  <- c(2035, 2064)   # Mid-century future period (30 years)

in_hist   <- function(yr) yr >= hist_yrs[1] & yr <= hist_yrs[2]
in_fut    <- function(yr) yr >= fut_yrs[1]  & yr <= fut_yrs[2]
in_window <- function(yr) in_hist(yr) | in_fut(yr)

# --- 7. Utility Functions ---

# Downloaded inputs are saved here the first time they are pulled, so later
# runs read the saved copy instead of re-downloading. Set refresh = TRUE in a
# call (or delete the file) to pull a fresh copy.
report_data_dir <- "data/park/GLAC/report_data"
tables_dir      <- "data/park/GLAC/tables"
dir.create(report_data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(tables_dir,      recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Helper: download once, then reuse the saved copy.
# Rasters are saved as GeoTIFFs; everything else as .rds.
cache_download <- function(name, expr, refresh = FALSE) {
  rds_path <- file.path(report_data_dir, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  tif_path <- file.path(report_data_dir, paste0(name, ".tif"))
  if (!refresh && file.exists(tif_path)) return(terra::rast(tif_path))
  if (!refresh && file.exists(rds_path)) return(readRDS(rds_path))
  out <- expr
  # Don't save failed or empty downloads, so the next run tries again
  if (is.null(out) || (is.atomic(out) && all(is.na(out))) ||
      (is.data.frame(out) && nrow(out) == 0)) {
    warning("cache_download('", name, "'): download returned no data; not saved")
    return(out)
  }
  if (inherits(out, "RasterLayer")) out <- terra::rast(out)
  if (inherits(out, "SpatRaster")) {
    terra::writeRaster(out, tif_path, overwrite = TRUE)
    return(terra::rast(tif_path))
  }
  saveRDS(out, rds_path)
  out
}

# Helper: save a tabulated output as a CSV in the tables directory.
save_table <- function(df, name) {
  out <- as.data.frame(df)
  # Keep row names (e.g., transposed summary tables) as a first column
  if (!identical(rownames(out), as.character(seq_len(nrow(out))))) {
    out <- tibble::rownames_to_column(out, "row")
  }
  readr::write_csv(out, file.path(tables_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")))
  invisible(df)
}


# Format axis labels as "Xk" (thousands)
k_formatter <- function(x) paste0(comma(x / 1000), "k")

# Filter a data frame to only the historical and mid-century future periods.
# Accepts either a numeric `year` column or a Date/POSIXct `date` column —
# if both are present, `year` takes precedence.
filter_analysis_periods <- function(df) {
  if ("year" %in% names(df) && is.numeric(df[["year"]])) {
    df %>% dplyr::filter(
      in_window(year)
    )
  } else if ("date" %in% names(df)) {
    df %>% dplyr::mutate(.yr_temp = lubridate::year(date)) %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        in_window(.yr_temp)
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(-.yr_temp)
  } else {
    stop("filter_analysis_periods: data frame must contain either a numeric `year` column or a Date/POSIXct `date` column.")
  }
}
```

Building on the previous section, this chunk defines the spatial extent of the 
study and retrieves the necessary administrative and infrastructure layers from 
the NPS DataStore.

We define the primary study area using 4-digit NPS Unit Code 
(<https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/foia/upload/NPS-Unit-List.xlsx>) and retrieve 
spatial boundaries and building footprints.

```{r park_dat}
# --- 1. Define Study Unit ---
# Glacier National Park (GLAC)
park <- "GLAC"

# --- 2. Retrieve Administrative Boundaries ---
# Fetch park geometry and metadata from the NPS IRMA DataStore
park_boundary <- cache_download("park_boundary", getParkBoundary(park = park))
state         <- park_boundary$STATE

# --- 3. Infrastructure and Hydrology ---
# Retrieve building footprints intersecting the park boundary
buildings <- cache_download("buildings", getBuildings(park_boundary, dist = 0))

# Delineate the recharge (contributing) area for the Logan Pass infiltration
# gallery from the USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DTM (Montana Statewide Phase 2, 2020,
# with gaps filled from Phase 3, 2021) using whitebox, as done at MORA.
logan_infil <- st_read("data/park/GLAC/logan_infil.shp", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_zm()

# Read only a clipped window of the cloud-optimized lidar tiles: the gallery
# plus 1.5 km, which covers the full catchment up to the Garden Wall ridge
lidar_dir <- "data/park/GLAC/Lidar"
lidar_dem_path <- file.path(lidar_dir, "lidar_DTM_logan_pass.tif")
lidar_base <- "/vsicurl/https://prd-tnm.s3.amazonaws.com/StagedProducts/Elevation/1m/Projects/"
lidar_tiles <- c(
  "MT_Statewide_Phase2_2020_B20/TIFF/USGS_1M_12_x29y540_MT_Statewide_Phase2_2020_B20.tif",
  "MT_Statewide_Phase2_2020_B20/TIFF/USGS_1M_12_x30y540_MT_Statewide_Phase2_2020_B20.tif",
  "MT_Statewide_Phase3_2021_B21/TIFF/USGS_1M_12_x29y540_MT_Statewide_Phase3_2021_B21.tif",
  "MT_Statewide_Phase3_2021_B21/TIFF/USGS_1M_12_x30y540_MT_Statewide_Phase3_2021_B21.tif")
if (!file.exists(lidar_dem_path)) {
  lidar_window <- logan_infil %>% st_transform(26912) %>% st_buffer(1500) %>% vect()
  # merge() gives earlier rasters priority, so 2020 is primary and 2021 fills gaps
  lidar_dem <- purrr::map(lidar_tiles, ~ crop(rast(paste0(lidar_base, .x)), lidar_window)) %>%
    unname() %>%
    do.call(merge, .)
  # Plain DEFLATE: whitebox can't read floating-point predictor compression
  writeRaster(lidar_dem, lidar_dem_path, gdal = "COMPRESS=DEFLATE", overwrite = TRUE)
}

# Whitebox writes its intermediates to disk, so use an absolute output path.
# auto_snap moves the gallery point onto the main flow line (~10 m away)
# so the chunk knits without the interactive click used at MORA.
dir.create(file.path(lidar_dir, "whitebox"), showWarnings = FALSE)
recharge_area <- cache_download("lidar_watershed", delineate_watershed(
  dem              = rast(lidar_dem_path),
  pour_point       = logan_infil,
  output_dir       = normalizePath(file.path(lidar_dir, "whitebox")),
  file_prefix      = "logan_gallery",
  breach_dist      = 10,
  snap_buffer_dist = 10,
  interactive_snap = FALSE,
  auto_snap        = TRUE,
  write_gpkg       = TRUE,
  crs_out          = "EPSG:26912")) %>%  # native lidar CRS, avoids resampling
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary))

# --- 4. Logan Pass Supply and Demand Data ---
# Load daily supply/demand records provided by the park.
logan_sd <- read_csv("data/park/GLAC/logan_pass_supply_demand.csv") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date       = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%y"),
    supply_gal = as.numeric(supply_gal),
    use_gal    = as.numeric(use_gal)
  ) %>%
  # Three days have recorded use ~10x the surrounding days (40,000-75,000 gal),
  # far beyond what the 10,000-gal tank and 4-8 gpm gallery can deliver. These
  # are attributed to data-entry errors (an extra digit) and are corrected by
  # dividing by 10. Days of 10,000-12,500 gal are plausible (the 2009 EA reports
  # peaks up to 12,000 gpd) and are kept.
  dplyr::mutate(
    use_gal = ifelse(use_gal > 20000, use_gal / 10, use_gal)
  )

# Monthly aggregation
logan_sd_monthly <- logan_sd %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    supply_gal   = sum(supply_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    use_gal      = sum(use_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_days_data  = n(),
    days_in_month = days_in_month(first(ym))
  )

# Annual aggregation (used for figure labels and trend lines)
logan_sd_annual <- logan_sd %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    avg_supply = mean(supply_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_use    = mean(use_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Mid-year date for label placement
    label_date = as.Date(paste0(unique(year), "-08-01")),
    .groups    = "drop"
  )
```

### 2. Identify the water supplies

In this section, we extract the site-specific water supply information and 
delineate the hydrological boundaries for the Logan Pass system.

##### ---- Water Supply Database

We utilize a comprehensive NPS database to isolate water supply sources for the 
study unit and perform a spatial join to identify their respective watersheds. 
The database contains a row for each water supply system and source of water 
(e.g., individual wells, diversions, and springs).

```{r water_supply_db}

# Import database and convert to spatial (sf) object
WSD <- cache_download("water_supply_database", get_wsd()) %>%
  dplyr::filter(park_unit == park)

# --- 2. Target Site Selection ---
# Filter for Logan Pass infrastructure
select_sources <- WSD %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Logan", water_system_name))

# --- 3. Watershed Delineation ---
# Delineate watersheds for each selected source using point locations
select_sources <- select_sources %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    watershed = purrr::map(
      .x = 1:nrow(.),
      .f = ~ cache_download(paste0("auto_watershed_", .x),
                            getXYWatersheds(sf = select_sources[.x, ], coordinates = NULL, snap = TRUE))
    )
  )

# --- 4. Spatial Visualization: Park-Wide Systems ---
mapview(park_boundary,
        col.regions  = "seagreen",
        alpha.regions = 0.2,
        color        = "white",
        lwd          = 3,
        layer.name   = "Park Boundary") +
  mapview(WSD,
          zcol       = "source_type",
          layer.name = "All Water Sources") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions  = "yellow",
          alpha.regions = 0,
          color        = "yellow",
          lwd          = 4,
          cex          = 8,
          layer.name   = "Selected Project Sources")

# --- 5. Spatial Visualization: Logan Pass Focus ---
# Filter buildings within 1 km of the selected sources
sel_bldg <- cache_download("buildings_buffer", getBuildings(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(st_buffer(st_transform(select_sources, st_crs(buildings)), 1000))

#mapview(select_sources$watershed,
#        color        = "dodgerblue",
#        alpha.regions = 0.1,
#        col.regions  = "dodgerblue",
#        lwd          = 2,
#        layer.name   = "Auto-Delineated Rch. Area") +
  mapview(recharge_area,
          color        = "navy",
          alpha.regions = 0.1,
          col.regions  = "navy",
          lwd          = 2,
          layer.name   = "Lidar-Delineated Rch. Area") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions  = "yellow",
          alpha.regions = 1,
          color        = "yellow",
          lwd          = 4,
          cex          = 8,
          layer.name   = "Logan Pass Infiltration Gallery") +
  mapview(sel_bldg,
          col.regions = "gray40",
          layer.name  = "Nearby Infrastructure")
```



#### ----- Weather stations

In this section, we retrieve historical climatological data from the NOAA Global
Historical Climatology Network (GHCN) for stations within and surrounding 
Glacier National Park. The raw data is processed to standardize units and 
summarized into monthly and annual water-year aggregates.

```{r weather_stations}
# --- 1. Retrieve NOAA Weather Data ---
# Buffer park boundary by 5 km to capture representative peripheral stations
noaa <- cache_download("noaa", getNOAA(st_buffer(park_boundary, 5000), "GLAC")) %>%
  st_transform(4326)

# Extract a metadata list of unique stations (one row per station)
stations <- noaa %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup()

# --- 2. Data Cleaning and Unit Conversion ---
# GHCN data often scales values (e.g., Temp * 10); we revert to standard units
weather_data <- noaa %>%
  dplyr::select(name, id, date, prcp, snow, snwd, tmax, tmin, tobs) %>%
  # Reconvert values stored as tenths (mm * 0.1 to mm, C * 0.1 to C)
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax", "tmin", "prcp"), ~ .x * 0.10) %>%
  # Convert Millimeters to Inches
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("snow", "snwd", "prcp"), ~ .x * 0.0393701) %>%
  # Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax", "tmin"), ~ (9 / 5) * .x + 32)

# --- 3. Monthly Summaries and Accumulation ---
weather_data_mon <- weather_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ym   = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7)),
    year = year(date)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, name, id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    tmax  = max(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    tmin  = min(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
    tmean = mean(c(tmax, tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp  = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
    snow  = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
    snwd  = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Date = ym) %>%
  addWaterYear() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(waterYear, name) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    prcp_cum = cumsum(prcp),
    snow_cum = cumsum(snow),
    snwd_cum = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Melt proxy: cumulative snowfall minus current snow depth
    melt     = snow_cum - snwd
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# --- 4. Annual Water Year Summaries ---
weather_data_an <- weather_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(waterYear = calc_water_year(date, water_year_start_month = 10)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(waterYear, name, id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    tmax  = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    tmin  = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
    tmean = mean(c(tmax, tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
    prcp  = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
    snow  = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
    snwd  = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- 5. Selection and Visualization ---
# Target stations with long-term reliable records for Logan Pass context
select_station_list <- c("USS0013A19S", "USS0013A27S")

# Map selected stations by elevation
mapview(stations %>%
          dplyr::filter(id %in% select_station_list) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(elevation_ft = elevation / 0.3048),
        zcol       = "elevation_ft",
        layer.name = "Station Elevation (ft)") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions = "tomato",
          cex        = 10,
          layer.name = "Water Sources")

# Plot annual trends for selected meteorological variables
ggplot(weather_data_an %>%
         dplyr::filter(id %in% select_station_list) %>%
         pivot_longer(cols = c("tmax", "tmin", "tmean", "prcp", "snwd"),
                      names_to  = "vars",
                      values_to = "vals"),
       aes(x = waterYear, y = vals, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(lwd = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~vars, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_colorblind("Station Name") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Water Year", y = "Value (Standard Units)")

# --- 6. Cleanup ---
rm(noaa, weather_data)
gc()
```

#### ----- SNOTEL

In this segment, we retrieve and process data from the SNOTEL (Snow Telemetry) 
network. SNOTEL stations provide critical high-elevation data, including Snow 
Water Equivalent (SWE, reported from SNOTEL as "wteq" variable), essential for understanding snowmelt recharge timing at Logan Pass.

```{r snotel}
# --- 1. Retrieve SNOTEL Data ---
# Search for SNOTEL sites within 20 km of the recharge area boundary
snotel <- cache_download("snotel", getSNOTEL(
  aoi  = recharge_area %>% dplyr::mutate(Name = "Recharge Area"),
  dist = 20000,
  years = "all"
)) %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%   # tidy as a plain table; site points are rebuilt from latitude/longitude below
  clean_names()

# Extract unique station metadata for mapping
snotel_sites <- snotel %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)

# --- 2. Spatial Visualization: Station Locations ---
mapview(park_boundary,
        alpha.regions = 0.1,
        layer.name    = "Park Boundary") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions = "red",
          layer.name  = "Water Sources") +
  mapview(snotel_sites,
          col.regions = "darkblue",
          layer.name  = "SNOTEL Sites")

# --- 3. Tidy and Pivot Sensor Data ---
snotel_tidy <- snotel %>%
  dplyr::filter(sensor_id %in% c("PREC.I", "SNWD.I", "WTEQ.I")) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, name, value, sensor_id, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    across(c(value, water_year), as.numeric), 
    date = as.Date(date)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date, name, sensor_id, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sensor_id, values_from = value) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    prec_mm = prec_i * 0.1,
    prec_in = prec_mm * 0.0393701
  )

# --- 4. Monthly and Annual Summarization ---
snotel_m <- snotel_tidy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    snwd = max(snwd_i, na.rm = TRUE),
    prec = sum(prec_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    wteq = max(wteq_i, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

snotel_annual <- snotel_tidy %>%
  dplyr::group_by(name, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    wteq = max(wteq_i, na.rm = TRUE),
    prec = sum(prec_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    snwd = max(snwd_i, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# --- 5. Visualization: Annual SWE Trends ---
# Pre-calculate the 5th quantiles for the specific sites
thresholds <- snotel_annual %>%
  dplyr::filter(name %in% c("Flattop Mtn.", "Many Glacier")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(q05 = quantile(wteq, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
                   q10 = quantile(wteq, 0.1, na.rm = TRUE))

# Build the plot
ggplot(snotel_annual, aes(x = water_year, y = wteq, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3, lwd = 0.8) +
  
  # Add horizontal lines using the pre-calculated thresholds
  geom_hline(data = thresholds, 
             aes(yintercept = q10, color = name), 
             linetype = "dashed", lwd = 0.8) +
  
  # Add text labels just above the lines
  geom_text(data = thresholds, 
            aes(x = min(snotel_annual$water_year), y = q10, 
                label = paste("10th percentile:", round(q10, 1), "in")),
            hjust = 0, vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_colorblind("SNOTEL Site") +
  labs(title = "Annual Maximum Snow Water Equivalent (SWE)",
       x = "Water Year",
       y = "Max SWE (inches)",
       color = "SNOTEL Site") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/Snotel_sites.jpg", width = 7, height = 3, dpi = 600)


# Evaluate swe to precip ratio
swe_summary <- snotel_annual %>%
  dplyr::mutate(swe_frac_of_precip = wteq/prec) %>%
  # remove outlier values > 1 at start of series
  dplyr::filter(water_year > 1980) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(name) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    swe_frac_of_precip = mean(swe_frac_of_precip)
  ) %>%
  print()

ggplot(snotel_annual, aes(x = water_year, y = wteq/prec, color = name)) + geom_line() +
geom_smooth()

# --- 6. Memory Cleanup ---
rm(snotel)
gc()
```

#### ----- USGS Surface Water

In this section, we analyze surface water dynamics using USGS NWIS data. Stream 
gages near Glacier National Park establish baseline hydrological regimes and 
identify shifts in snowmelt timing and magnitude.

```{r usgs_SW, eval = TRUE}
# --- 1. Identify Nearby Stream Gages ---
bbox_vals <- sf::st_bbox(park_boundary) %>%
  as.numeric() %>%
  round(digits = 5)

# Retrieve monitoring locations and calculate distance to water sources
usgs_sw <- cache_download("usgs_stream_sites", read_waterdata_monitoring_location(bbox = bbox_vals, 
                                              site_type = "Stream")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(park_boundary) %>%
  mutate(dist_m = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, st_transform(select_sources, st_crs(park_boundary)))))

# Select the 15 nearest sites for initial screening
nearest_usgs_sw <- usgs_sw %>%
  slice_min(order_by = dist_m, n = 15)

# --- 2. Retrieve Daily Discharge Data ---
usgs_discharge <- cache_download("usgs_discharge_daily", read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = nearest_usgs_sw$monitoring_location_id,
  parameter_code         = "00060"  # Discharge, cubic feet per second
))

# Refine station list based on successful data retrieval
nearest_usgs_sw <- nearest_usgs_sw %>%
  dplyr::filter(monitoring_location_id %in% unique(usgs_discharge$monitoring_location_id))

# distance to Logan Pass
nearest_usgs_sw %>% select(monitoring_location_name, dist_m) %>% print()

# Join station metadata to discharge records
usgs_discharge <- usgs_discharge %>%
  left_join(
    nearest_usgs_sw %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::select(monitoring_location_id, monitoring_location_name, altitude, agency_code),
    by = "monitoring_location_id"
  )

# --- 3. Helper: Clean station name abbreviations ---
clean_names_fn <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("nr. |nr ",   "near ",      monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("C |Cr ",     "Creek ",     monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("ab ",        "above ",     monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("Lk ",        "Lake ",      monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("G ",         "Grinnell ",  monitoring_location_name)
  )
}

# --- 4. Process Hydrographs: Split into "early" and "late" periods ---
usgs_discharge_doy <- usgs_discharge %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(time) > 1957) %>%
  clean_names_fn() %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_name) %>%
  mutate(
    global_start = min(time),
    global_end   = max(time),
    period       = ifelse(time < global_start + (global_end - global_start) / 2,
                          "early", "late")
  ) %>%
  group_by(doy = yday(time), monitoring_location_name, period) %>%
  summarize(
    p_start      = min(time),
    p_end        = max(time),
    discharge    = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    discharge_min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    discharge_max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31"))

# --- 5. Extract 2025 Observations ---
usgs_discharge_doy_2025 <- usgs_discharge %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(time) == 2025) %>%
  clean_names_fn() %>%
  group_by(doy = yday(time), monitoring_location_name) %>%
  summarize(discharge = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31"), period = "2025")

usgs_discharge_wy <- usgs_discharge_doy %>%
  mutate(
    # Create a date that shifts Oct-Dec to the previous 'dummy' year
    # so the axis naturally starts at October
    wy_date = if_else(month(doy_date) >= 10, 
                      doy_date %m-% years(1), 
                      doy_date)
  )

# 2. Apply the same logic to your 2025 data
usgs_2025_wy <- usgs_discharge_doy_2025 %>%
  mutate(wy_date = if_else(month(doy_date) >= 10, 
                           doy_date %m-% years(1), 
                           doy_date))


# --- 6. Build Facet Labels ---
facet_labels <- usgs_discharge_doy %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_name, period) %>%
  summarize(p_min = min(p_start), p_max = max(p_end), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(period_string = paste0(period, ": ", format(p_min, "%Y"), "-", format(p_max, "%Y"))) %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_name) %>%
  summarize(
    full_label = paste(period_string, collapse = "\n"),
    x_pos      = as.Date("2020-01-01"),
    y_pos      = Inf,
    .groups    = "drop"
  )

# --- 7. Plot: All Stations ---
ggplot(usgs_discharge_doy, aes(x = doy_date, color = period, fill = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = discharge_min, ymax = discharge_max), alpha = 0.4, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = discharge), lwd = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = facet_labels,
            aes(x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label = full_label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.3, size = 2.8, lineheight = 0.9) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_color_manual("Period", values = c("early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
  scale_fill_manual("Period",  values = c("early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
  facet_wrap(~monitoring_location_name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Historical Discharge Regimes: Early vs. Late Records",
       x = "Day of Year", y = "Discharge (cfs)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 7))

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/usgs_discharge_regional.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 10, height = 7)

# --- 8. Plot: 2025 Focus (Swiftcurrent Creek) ---

ggplot(usgs_discharge_wy %>%
         filter(monitoring_location_name == "Swiftcurrent Creek at Many Glacier MT"),
       aes(x = wy_date, color = period, fill = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = discharge_min, ymax = discharge_max), alpha = 0.4, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = discharge), lwd = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = usgs_2025_wy %>%
              filter(monitoring_location_name == "Swiftcurrent Creek at Many Glacier MT"),
            aes(x = wy_date, y = discharge, color = "2025"), lwd = 1) +
  # ... [Your geom_text remains similar, just update x = x_pos if it's date-based] ...
  theme_bw() +
  # This scale will now naturally start in October
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", 
               date_labels = "%b",

  scale_fill_manual("Period",  values = c("2025" = "black", "early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
```

#### ----- USGS Groundwater

In this segment, we examine groundwater levels. Monitoring groundwater elevation (NAVD88) and converting it to depth-to-water provides insight into aquifer storage supporting the park's water systems.

```{r USGS_gw}
# --- 1. Identify Groundwater Monitoring Wells ---
bbox_vals <- sf::st_bbox(park_boundary) %>%
  as.numeric() %>%
  round(digits = 5)

usgs_groundwater <- cache_download("usgs_well_sites", read_waterdata_monitoring_location(bbox = bbox_vals, site_type = "Well")) %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(park_boundary) %>%
  # Only keep wells with a vertical datum for elevation-to-depth calculations
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vertical_datum))

# --- 2. Retrieve Field Measurements ---
# Parameter 62611 = groundwater elevation above datum (ft)
usgs_groundwater_levels <-
  cache_download("usgs_well_field_measurements", dataRetrieval::read_waterdata_field_measurements(
    monitoring_location_id = usgs_groundwater$monitoring_location_id,
    parameter_code         = "62611"
  )) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date    = as.Date(time),
    site_no = sub("USGS-", "", monitoring_location_id),
    ym      = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) >= 1900) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, monitoring_location_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_lev = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(monitoring_location_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dev_mean = mean_lev - mean(mean_lev, na.rm = TRUE),
    count    = n()
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(count > 1)

# --- 3. Calculate Depth-to-Water ---
# Subset wells to those with level data, then join surface elevations
usgs_groundwater <- usgs_groundwater %>%
  dplyr::filter(monitoring_location_id %in% unique(usgs_groundwater_levels$monitoring_location_id))

usgs_groundwater_levels <- usgs_groundwater_levels %>%
  left_join(
    usgs_groundwater %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
      dplyr::select(monitoring_location_id, altitude),
    by = "monitoring_location_id"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gw_depth_ft = altitude - mean_lev)

# --- 4. Visualization: Groundwater Depth Trends ---
colfunc <- colorRampPalette(c(pal$yellow, pal$darkblue, pal$orange, pal$pink, pal$black))

ggplot(usgs_groundwater_levels,
       aes(x = ym, y = gw_depth_ft, col = monitoring_location_id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_reverse() +  # Standard convention: depth increases downward
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Groundwater Depth Trends",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Depth Below Surface (ft)") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = colfunc(nrow(usgs_groundwater)))

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/usgs_gw_depths_2025.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 6, height = 4)
```

### 4. Climate and Water Balance

In this section, we transition from historical observations to future climate projections. By leveraging the CMIP5 multi-model ensemble, we identify specific GCMs that represent the diverging "Hot Dry" and "Warm Wet" climate futures for the Glacier National Park region.

#### - GCM Selection

```{r gcm_skill}
# Load GCM regional skill rankings for the Pacific Northwest region (PWR),
# the Rupp et al. region that includes Glacier National Park
all_cfs <- cache_download("GCM_skill_by_region", read_delim("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rossyndicate/CCRP_automated_climate_futures/master/data/general/GCM_skill_by_region.txt")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Region == "PWR") %>%
  # Standardize naming for HadGEM model variants
  dplyr::mutate(
    GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-ES.", "HadGEM2-ES365.", GCM),
    GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-CC.", "HadGEM2-CC365.", GCM)
  ) %>%
  # Apply Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP 4.5 and 8.5)
  tidyr::crossing(data.table(RCP = c("rcp45", "rcp85"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    GCM   = paste0(GCM, RCP),
    Skill = ifelse(Rank > 18, "Low Skill", "High Skill")
  )
```


#### - Download climate data

In this section, we acquire the high-resolution climate datasets necessary for driving the water balance models. We integrate historical GridMET data (4 km resolution) with future MACA-downscaled GCM projections, subset to the Logan Pass recharge area.

#### - Run WBM

In this stage, we execute the NPS Water Balance Model (WBM) to translate meteorological inputs into hydrological outputs (snowpack, soil moisture, AET).

The `hock_coef` is calibrated to 3 (standard default is 4), which better captures snow accumulation and melt timing at SNOTEL sites in this high-elevation western terrain.

```{r wbm_run}
# --- 1. Parameterization ---
# Load essential environmental rasters (AWC, latitude, etc.) for the WBM
load_wbm_rasters(crs = crs(clim_pts))

# Calibrated Hock coefficient (default = 4; regional SNOTEL calibration → 3)
hock <- 3

# Shared WBM arguments (applied to both historical and future runs)
wbm_base_args <- list(
  Direct_Frac     = 0,
  Return_Rate     = 1,
  PET_Method      = "Oudin",
  hock_coef       = hock,
  Snowpack.Init   = 0,
  Soil.Init       = 0,
  Shade.Coeff     = 1,
  T.Base          = 0,
  Soil_mult       = 1,
  PET_mult        = 1,
  area_weighted   = FALSE,
  aoi             = recharge_area,  # only used when area_weighted = TRUE
  grid            = aoi_gridmet_grid,
  aggregate       = FALSE
)

# --- 2. Historical Baseline Run ---
recharge_wbm <- exec(
  run_NPS_WBM_points,
  points         = clim_pts, 
  climate_data   = clim_hist, 
  ret_final_cond = TRUE,
  !!!wbm_base_args  #"bang-bang-bang" operator splices the list of base args
)

# --- 3. Extract Final Conditions to Seed Future Runs ---
# Use the final soil and snowpack levels from 2024 as starting conditions for 2025+
final_cond <- recharge_wbm[[2]] #%>%
  #dplyr::select(x, y, final_soil, final_snowpack)

clim_pts_fc <- clim_pts %>%
  dplyr::left_join(final_cond, by = c("x", "y"))

recharge_wbm <- recharge_wbm[[1]]

# --- Optional: Hock Coefficient Calibration Check ---
# Set test_hock = TRUE to visually compare WBM snowpack to SNOTEL observations
test_hock <- FALSE

if (test_hock) {
  ggplot(
    snotel_tidy %>%
      dplyr::filter(name == "Flattop Mtn.") %>%
      dplyr::select(date, wteq_i) %>%
      left_join(recharge_wbm %>% dplyr::select(date, snowpack_in_wbm, x, y), by = "date") %>%
      dplyr::filter(year(date) == 2020) %>%
      dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(mean_snowpack = mean(snowpack_in_wbm)),
    aes(x = date)
  ) +
    geom_line(aes(y = snowpack_in_wbm, color = "WBM GRID", group = paste0(x, y)), lwd = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(y = mean_snowpack,   color = "WBM MEAN"), lwd = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(y = wteq_i,          color = "SNOTEL"),   lwd = 1) +
    labs(x = "", y = "Snowpack (in)") +
    annotate("text", label = paste0("Hock Coef: ", hock),
             y = Inf, x = -Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_color_manual("", values = c("black", "lightblue", "red"))

  ggsave(paste0("data/park/GLAC/Figs/Hock_", hock, ".jpg"), width = 5, height = 3, dpi = 600)
}

# --- 4. Future Projection Run ---

recharge_fut_wbm <- exec(
  run_NPS_WBM_points,
  points         = clim_pts_fc,
  climate_data   = clim_fut,
  ret_final_cond = FALSE,
  param_list     = final_cond,
  use_final      = TRUE,
  !!!wbm_base_args
)

#rm(clim_fut, clim_hist)
gc()
```


##### - Routing

Apply a routing function to WBM runoff to better represent the available supply 
at the infiltration gallery.

Water is sourced from snowmelt and precip runoff captured by an infiltration 
gallery along the slopes of Clements and Oberlin mountains. The WBM runoff term
represents all runoff in the contributing area, but a significant fraction exits
via Oberlin Creek or flows past the gallery as shallow groundwater. We:

a) Apply a scaling factor to match total captured volume, and  
b) Apply a routing function to reflect the continuous nature of subsurface 
flow into the gallery.

```{r routing_functions}
# --- Routing Parameter Configuration ---

# Runoff scale factor: multiplied against WBM runoff to match observed supply volumes.
# Tested across 0.0026 – 0.46; values above 0.026 produce implausibly high volumes.
runoff_scale <- 0.007739


# Calibrated routing parameters (manual calibration; see chunk `automated_cal_NOT_RUN`)
tau_q <- 3    # Quick-flow recession constant (days)
tau_s <- 120   # Slow-flow recession constant (days)
vs    <- 0.7  # Fraction of storage routed as slow flow

# --- Wrapper: apply routing with calibrated parameters ---
# Takes a data.table with columns `date` and `runoff_col_name`, returns the
# routed inflow column (vector, second column of routing output).
apply_routing <- function(df, runoff_col) {
  runoff_routing_gw(
    df                = df,
    runoff_col        = runoff_col,
    date_col          = "date",
    tau_q             = tau_q,
    tau_s             = tau_s,
    vs                = vs,
    loss              = 0,
    baseflow          = 0,
    delay             = 0,
    slow_only         = TRUE,
    return_components = FALSE,
    max_inf           = 5000
  )[, 2]
}

# --- 1. Runoff Scaling and Data Preparation ---
# Temporary subset restricted to years overlapping with Logan Pass station data
mod_dat <- recharge_wbm %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(runoff_in_wbm = mean(runoff_in_wbm)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% c(2015, unique(year(logan_sd$date)))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Convert runoff depth to volume (inches → cubic feet → gallons)
    runoff_gal = runoff_scale * cf_to_gal * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, runoff_gal) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::left_join(logan_sd, by = "date") %>%
  # Apply 7-day centered rolling mean to smooth noise in supply signal
  dplyr::mutate(
    supply_gal = frollmean(supply_gal, n = 7, align = "center", fill = mean(supply_gal))
  )

cal_dat <- mod_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% c(2016))

# --- 2. Manual Model Calibration (Visual Check) ---
inflow_manual <- apply_routing(
  df         = as.data.table(mod_dat %>% dplyr::select(date, runoff_gal)),
  runoff_col = "runoff_gal"
)

inflow_manual <- runoff_routing_gw(
  df                = mod_dat,
  runoff_col        = "runoff_gal",
  date_col          = "date",
  tau_q             = tau_q,
  tau_s             = tau_s,
  vs                = vs,
  slow_only         = TRUE,
  delay             = 0,
  loss              = 0,
  return_components = TRUE,
  max_inf           = 5000
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(mod_dat %>% dplyr::select(date, supply_gal, use_gal, runoff_gal), by = "date") %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) > 2015)

# Peak discharge dates (June–September) used for vertical lines on plot
peak_dates <- inflow_manual %>%
  dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% 6:9) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Q_tot == max(Q_tot, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, year) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1)

ggplot(inflow_manual %>%
         dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% 6:9) %>%
         dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)),
       aes(x = date)) +
  geom_vline(data = peak_dates,
             aes(xintercept = date, group = year),
             color = pal$darkblue, lwd = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(y = use_gal,    color = "Reported Use"),    size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = supply_gal, color = "Reported Supply"), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q_tot,       color = "WBM + Routing (Total Flow)"),   size = 0.9) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q_slow,      color = "WBM + Routing (Baseflow)"),          size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~year, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Reported Supply" = "#000000",
    "WBM + Routing (Total Flow)"   = pal$darkblue,
    "WBM"             = pal$lightblue,
    "Reported Use"    = "red",
    "WBM + Routing (Baseflow)"          = pal$lightblue
  )) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x     = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(title    = "Comparison of Modeled and Observed Supply",
       subtitle = "June – September System Dynamics",
       y        = "Flow (Gallons per Day)")

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/flow_calibration_supply_demand.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 6)
```




```{r routing_ensemble}
# --- Routing Parameter Ensemble Configuration ---

# Define plausible parameter ranges 
param_grid <- expand.grid(
  runoff_scale = c(0.00516, 0.01032, 0.01548),
  tau_q        = c(2, 3, 5, 8),          # Quick-flow recession constant (days)
  tau_s        = c(60, 90, 120, 180),    # Slow-flow recession constant (days)
  vs           = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8)  # Fraction of storage routed as slow flow
)

cat(sprintf("Testing %d parameter combinations...\n", nrow(param_grid)))

# --- Wrapper: apply routing for a given parameter set ---
apply_routing_params <- function(df, runoff_col, tau_q, tau_s, vs) {
  runoff_routing_gw(
    df                = df,
    runoff_col        = runoff_col,
    date_col          = "date",
    tau_q             = tau_q,
    tau_s             = tau_s,
    vs                = vs,
    loss              = 0,
    baseflow          = 0,
    delay             = 0,
    slow_only         = TRUE,
    return_components = FALSE,
    max_inf           = 5000
  )[, 2]
}

# --- 1. Base Data Preparation (shared across all parameter combinations) ---
# Prepare base runoff data — scale factor applied per-iteration below
base_dat <- recharge_wbm %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(runoff_in_wbm = mean(runoff_in_wbm)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% c(2015, unique(year(logan_sd$date)))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::left_join(logan_sd, by = "date") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    supply_gal = frollmean(supply_gal, n = 7, align = "center", fill = mean(supply_gal))
  )

# --- 2. Ensemble Run: sweep all parameter combinations ---
ensemble_results <- purrr::map_dfr(
  seq_len(nrow(param_grid)),
  function(i) {
    p <- param_grid[i, ]

    df_iter <- base_dat %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        runoff_gal = p$runoff_scale * cf_to_gal * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(date, runoff_gal)

    Q_tot <- apply_routing_params(
      df         = as.data.table(df_iter),
      runoff_col = "runoff_gal",
      tau_q      = p$tau_q,
      tau_s      = p$tau_s,
      vs         = p$vs
    )

    data.frame(
      date         = base_dat$date,
      Q_tot        = Q_tot,
      runoff_scale = p$runoff_scale,
      tau_q        = p$tau_q,
      tau_s        = p$tau_s,
      vs           = p$vs,
      combo_id     = i
    )
  }
)

# --- 3. Summarize: min, max, mean across all parameter combinations ---
ensemble_summary <- ensemble_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) > 2015) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    Q_mean = mean(Q_tot, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q_min  = min(Q_tot,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Q_max  = max(Q_tot,  na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    base_dat %>%
      dplyr::filter(year(date) > 2015) %>%
      dplyr::select(date, supply_gal, use_gal),
    by = "date"
  )

# --- 4. Calibrated (best-fit) run for reference overlay ---
best_dat <- base_dat %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    runoff_gal = runoff_scale * cf_to_gal * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, runoff_gal)

best_fit <- apply_routing_params(
  df         = as.data.table(best_dat),
  runoff_col = "runoff_gal",
  tau_q      = 3,
  tau_s      = 120,
  vs         = 0.7
)

ensemble_summary <- ensemble_summary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Q_best = best_fit[year(base_dat$date) > 2015])

# --- 5. Peak discharge dates (June–September) for reference lines ---
peak_dates <- ensemble_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% 6:9) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Q_mean == max(Q_mean, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, year) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1)

# --- 6. Plot ensemble range with calibrated best-fit overlay ---
ggplot(
  ensemble_summary %>%
    dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% 6:9) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)),
  aes(x = date)
) +
  geom_vline(
    data        = peak_dates,
    aes(xintercept = date, group = year),
    color       = pal$darkblue, lwd = 0.5, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  # Ensemble range ribbon
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = Q_min, ymax = Q_max),
    fill  = pal$lightblue, alpha = 0.35
  ) +
  # Observed supply and use
  geom_point(aes(y = use_gal,    color = "Reported Use"),    size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = supply_gal, color = "Reported Supply"), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  # Ensemble mean and best-fit lines
  geom_line(aes(y = Q_mean, color = "Ensemble Mean"),      linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q_best, color = "Selected-fit (late-season match)"), linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~year, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Reported Supply"        = "#000000",
    "Reported Use"           = "red",
    "Ensemble Mean"          = pal$darkblue,
    "Selected-fit (late-season match)"  = "darkorange"
  )) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.title     = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x     = element_blank(),
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Ensemble Range of Modeled Inflow Across Parameter Combinations",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Shaded band = min/max across %d parameter sets | June–September",
      nrow(param_grid)
    ),
    y = "Flow (Gallons per Day)"
  )

ggsave(
  "data/park/GLAC/Figs/flow_calibration_ensemble_range.jpg",
  dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 6
)

# --- 7. Optional: export ensemble summary table ---
# write.csv(ensemble_summary, "data/park/GLAC/ensemble_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

##### - Select Climate Futures

We select a subset of GCMs that bound the uncertainty range at Glacier. We evaluate "Hot Dry" and "Warm Wet" futures as endmembers.

```{r cf_selection}

# --- Routing Parameter Sets ---
# Best-fit: manually calibrated values
params_best <- list(runoff_scale = 0.007739, tau_q = 3,  tau_s = 120, vs = 0.7)

# Low: parameter combination that minimises routed flow
# (lowest scale factor, fastest recession, lowest slow-flow fraction)
params_low  <- list(runoff_scale = 0.005160, tau_q = 8,  tau_s = 60,  vs = 0.5)

# High: parameter combination that maximises routed flow
# (highest scale factor, slowest recession, highest slow-flow fraction)
params_high <- list(runoff_scale = 0.02580, tau_q = 2,  tau_s = 180, vs = 0.8)

# --- Routing wrapper that accepts an explicit parameter set ---
apply_routing_p <- function(df, runoff_col, p) {
  runoff_routing_gw(
    df                = df,
    runoff_col        = runoff_col,
    date_col          = "date",
    tau_q             = p$tau_q,
    tau_s             = p$tau_s,
    vs                = p$vs,
    loss              = 0,
    baseflow          = 0,
    delay             = 0,
    slow_only         = TRUE,
    return_components = FALSE,
    max_inf           = 5000
  )[, 2]
}

# --- 1. Combine Historical and Future WBM Outputs ---
wbm_all <- recharge_wbm %>%
  bind_rows(recharge_fut_wbm %>% dplyr::filter(year(date) > 2025)) %>%
  as.data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tmean_F = (9 / 5 * tmean_C) + 32,
    # Pre-compute runoff volume at each scale factor — reused across three routing calls
    runoff_gal_best = params_best$runoff_scale * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
    runoff_gal_low  = params_low$runoff_scale  * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2 * cf_to_gal,
    runoff_gal_high = params_high$runoff_scale * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2 * cf_to_gal
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, x, y) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Best-fit routing (as before)
    inflow_gal     = apply_routing_p(data.table(date, runoff_gal_best), "runoff_gal_best", params_best),

    # Parametric low / high bounds
    inflow_gal_low  = apply_routing_p(data.table(date, runoff_gal_low),  "runoff_gal_low",  params_low),
    inflow_gal_high = apply_routing_p(data.table(date, runoff_gal_high), "runoff_gal_high", params_high),

    # Derived unit conversions
    inflow_cf      = inflow_gal     * gal_to_cf,
    inflow_cf_low  = inflow_gal_low  * gal_to_cf,
    inflow_cf_high = inflow_gal_high * gal_to_cf,

    # Operating-season (June–September) summaries
    seasonal_inflow_gal      = if_else(month(date) %in% 6:9, inflow_gal,      0),
    seasonal_inflow_gal_low  = if_else(month(date) %in% 6:9, inflow_gal_low,  0),
    seasonal_inflow_gal_high = if_else(month(date) %in% 6:9, inflow_gal_high, 0)
  ) %>%
  left_join(all_cfs, by = "GCM")

rm("recharge_fut_wbm", "recharge_wbm")
gc()

# --- 2. Calculate 30-Year Statistics for Each GCM ---
all_clim_stats <- wbm_all %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    year       = year(date),
    stat_period = case_when(
      in_hist(year) ~ "Baseline",
      in_fut(year)  ~ "Future",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period != "Other") %>%
  dplyr::select(GCM, stat_period, Skill, precip_in_wbm, tmean_C, runoff_in_wbm, pet_in_wbm, inflow_gal, inflow_gal_low, inflow_gal_high, seasonal_inflow_gal, seasonal_inflow_gal_low, seasonal_inflow_gal_high) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, stat_period, Skill) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_precip_in         = 365.25 * mean(precip_in_wbm),
    mean_tmean_C           = mean(tmean_C),
    mean_runoff_in         = 365.25 * mean(runoff_in_wbm),
    median_runoff_in       = quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.5),
    mean_inflow_gal        = 365.25 * mean(inflow_gal),
    mean_inflow_gal_low    = 365.25 * mean(inflow_gal_low),
    mean_inflow_gal_high.  = 365.25 * mean(inflow_gal_high),
    mean_seasonal_inflow_gal = 122 * mean(seasonal_inflow_gal), # June, July, Aug, Sept only so 122 days
    mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_low = 122 * mean(seasonal_inflow_gal_low),
    mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_high = 122 * mean(seasonal_inflow_gal_high),
    sd_runoff_in           = sd(runoff_in_wbm),
    cv_runoff_in           = sd(runoff_in_wbm) / mean(runoff_in_wbm),
    iqr_runoff_in          = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75)) -
                             as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.25)),
    q90_q10_runoff_in      = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.9)) -
                             as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.1)),
    peak_runoff_in         = max(runoff_in_wbm),
    mean_precip_minus_pet_in = mean(precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm),
    fract_zero_runoff      = sum(runoff_in_wbm == 0) / n(),
    .groups = "keep"
  )

baseline <- all_clim_stats %>% dplyr::filter(stat_period == "Baseline")
future   <- all_clim_stats %>% dplyr::filter(stat_period != "Baseline")

# --- 3. Calculate Future Differentials (future - baseline) ---
future_differentials <- future %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    delta_precip_in           = mean_precip_in - baseline$mean_precip_in,
    delta_tmean_C             = mean_tmean_C   - baseline$mean_tmean_C,
    delta_runoff_in           = mean_runoff_in - baseline$mean_runoff_in,
    delta_inflow_gal          = mean_inflow_gal - baseline$mean_inflow_gal,
    delta_seasonal_inflow_gal = mean_seasonal_inflow_gal - baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal,
    delta_seasonal_inflow_gal_low = mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_low - baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_low,
    delta_seasonal_inflow_gal_high = mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_high - baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_high,
    delta_seasonal_inflow_per = 100 * (mean_seasonal_inflow_gal - baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal) / baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal,
    delta_seasonal_inflow_low_per = 100 * (mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_low - baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_low) / baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_low,
    delta_seasonal_inflow_high_per = 100 * (mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_high - baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_high) / baseline$mean_seasonal_inflow_gal_high,
    delta_runoff_per          = 100 * (mean_runoff_in - baseline$mean_runoff_in) / baseline$mean_runoff_in,
    delta_precip_per          = 100 * (mean_precip_in - baseline$mean_precip_in) / baseline$mean_precip_in,
    delta_runoff_in_sd        = sd_runoff_in  - baseline$sd_runoff_in,
    delta_runoff_in_cv        = cv_runoff_in  - baseline$cv_runoff_in,
    delta_runoff_in_iqr       = iqr_runoff_in - baseline$iqr_runoff_in,
    delta_runoff_in_median    = median_runoff_in   - baseline$median_runoff_in,
    delta_runoff_q90_q10      = q90_q10_runoff_in  - baseline$q90_q10_runoff_in,
    delta_runoff_in_peak      = peak_runoff_in      - baseline$peak_runoff_in,
    delta_precip_minus_pet    = mean_precip_minus_pet_in - baseline$mean_precip_minus_pet_in,
    delta_fract_zero_runoff   = fract_zero_runoff   - baseline$fract_zero_runoff,
    centroid_cf               = ifelse(Skill == "Low Skill", "Low Skill", "Other"),
    RCP                       = str_sub(GCM, -5)
  )
```

Now, manually select climate future categories:

```{r cf_manual_select}
# Climate Future selection axes (temperature vs. precipitation)
x      <- "delta_tmean_C"
y      <- "delta_precip_in"
x_name <- "Temperature (C)"
y_name <- "Precipitation (in)"
high_x <- "Hot"
low_x  <- "Warm"
high_y <- "Wet"
low_y  <- "Dry"

selected_gcms <- select_cfs_deep_dive(
  df = future_differentials,
  x, y, x_name, y_name, high_x, low_x, high_y, low_y,
  to_plot = TRUE,
  region = "PWR",
  highlight = c("Hot Dry", "Warm Wet")
)

# Attach CF labels to future_differentials for downstream plots
future_differentials <- future_differentials %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    selected_gcms[[1]] %>%
      dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Hot Dry", "Warm Wet", "Hot Wet", "Warm Dry")) %>%
      dplyr::select(GCM, "select_CF" = CF),
    by = "GCM"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    GCM_Meta = case_when(
      centroid_cf == "Low Skill" ~ "Low Skill",
      !is.na(select_CF)          ~ select_CF,
      TRUE                       ~ "Other"
    )
  )
```

##### - Aggregate WBM

Filter to only selected CFs and compute routed inflow volumes across the full time series.

```{r subset_wbm}
# --- 1. Subset to Selected CFs ---
wbm <- wbm_all %>%
  data.table() %>%
  select(-c(Rank, Region, Skill, RCP, x, y, excess_water_in_wbm)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    selected_gcms[[1]] %>%
      dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Hot Dry", "Warm Wet")) %>%
      dplyr::select(CF, GCM),
    by = "GCM"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = ifelse(GCM == "GridMET", "Historical", CF)) %>%
  # 1979 is kept as the WBM spin-up year (excluded from statistics by the analysis windows)
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(CF), year(date) >= 1979) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date, CF, GCM) %>%
  # Average across grid cells to get a single AOI-mean time series
  dplyr::summarize(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tmean_F    = (9 / 5 * tmean_C) + 32,
    runoff_cf  = runoff_scale * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2,
    runoff_gal = runoff_cf * cf_to_gal
  )

rm(wbm_all)
gc()

# --- 2. Apply Routing to Runoff (Mid, Low, High uncertainty bounds) ---
# Mid uses the calibrated parameters (apply_routing(), `routing_functions`
# chunk); low and high use the tested parameter sets that minimize and
# maximize routed flow (params_low / params_high, `cf_selection` chunk), so
# the bounds match Table A1 and the 40-projection statistics.
wbm <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    runoff_gal_low  = params_low$runoff_scale  / runoff_scale * runoff_gal,
    runoff_gal_high = params_high$runoff_scale / runoff_scale * runoff_gal,
    inflow_gal      = apply_routing(data.table(date, runoff_gal), "runoff_gal"),
    inflow_gal_low  = apply_routing_p(data.table(date, runoff_gal_low),  "runoff_gal_low",  params_low),
    inflow_gal_high = apply_routing_p(data.table(date, runoff_gal_high), "runoff_gal_high", params_high),
    inflow_cf       = inflow_gal      * gal_to_cf,
    inflow_cf_low   = inflow_gal_low  * gal_to_cf,
    inflow_cf_high  = inflow_gal_high * gal_to_cf
  )

# --- 3. Define Aggregation Column Groups ---
mean_cols <- c("soil_in_wbm", "tmean_C", "tmean_F")
sum_cols  <- c("precip_in_wbm", "runoff_in_wbm", "rain_in_wbm",
               "snow_in_wbm", "melt_in_wbm", "aet_in_wbm", "pet_in_wbm",
               "runoff_cf", "runoff_gal", "inflow_gal", "inflow_gal_low",
               "inflow_gal_high", "inflow_cf")
max_cols  <- c("snowpack_in_wbm")

# --- 4. Annual and Monthly Summaries ---
wbm_annual <- wbm %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date), month = month(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year, GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Sum of June–September inflow (open season only)
    inflow_open_months_gal = sum(inflow_gal[month %in% 6:9], na.rm = TRUE),
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(sum_cols),  \(x) sum(x,  na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(max_cols),  \(x) max(x,  na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# Years with incomplete daily records (e.g., at the ends of the historical and
# future runs). These are dropped from annual figures only; all statistics use
# full-year analysis windows.
partial_years <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(CF, GCM, year, date) %>%
  dplyr::count(CF, year, name = "n_days") %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_days < 365) %>%
  dplyr::select(CF, year)

drop_partial_years <- function(df) {
  dplyr::anti_join(df, partial_years, by = c("CF", "year"))
}

wbm_monthly <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(sum_cols),  \(x) sum(x,  na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(max_cols),  \(x) max(x,  na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# --- 5. Print Percentage Change Summary ---
wbm_stats <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::filter(in_window(year)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    tmean_F               = mean(tmean_F),
    precip_in             = mean(precip_in_wbm),
    rain_in               = mean(rain_in_wbm),
    snow_in               = mean(snow_in_wbm),
    melt_in               = mean(melt_in_wbm),
    aet_in                = mean(aet_in_wbm),
    pet_in                = mean(pet_in_wbm),
    runoff_in             = mean(runoff_in_wbm),
    inflow_gal            = mean(inflow_gal),
    inflow_open_months_gal = mean(inflow_open_months_gal)
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric),
                ~ (. - .[CF == "Historical"]) / .[CF == "Historical"] * 100)) %>%
  filter(CF != "Historical")

print(wbm_stats)

# --- 6. Monthly Supply Proportion Distribution ---
monthly_supply_proportions <- wbm_monthly %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(CF, ym, inflow_gal, inflow_gal_low, inflow_gal_high) %>%
  mutate(
    month = month(ym),
    year  = year(ym),
    group = case_when(
      in_hist(year)                      ~ "Historical",
      in_fut(year)                       ~ "Future",
      TRUE                               ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  drop_na(group) %>%
  group_by(month, CF) %>%
  summarize(
    monthly_supply_gal     = mean(inflow_gal,      na.rm = TRUE),
    monthly_supply_gal_max = max(inflow_gal_high,  na.rm = TRUE),
    monthly_supply_gal_min = min(inflow_gal_low,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_date      = as_date(paste0("2000-", month, "-01")),
    month_days      = days_in_month(month_date)
  ) %>%
  group_by(CF) %>%
  mutate(
    total_gal        = sum(monthly_supply_gal),
    monthly_fraction = monthly_supply_gal / total_gal
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```


```{r wbm_stats}

wbm_stats <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::filter(in_window(year)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    tmean_F                = mean(tmean_F),

    snow_in                = mean(snow_in_wbm),
    melt_in                = mean(melt_in_wbm),

# Pull historical row as a named vector for reference
hist_vals <- wbm_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF == "Historical") %>%
  dplyr::select(-CF) %>%
  as.numeric()

var_names <- wbm_stats %>%
  dplyr::select(-CF) %>%
  names()

# Build long-format table: one row per variable
wbm_stats_long <- tibble::tibble(
  Variable = var_names,
  Historical = hist_vals
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    wbm_stats %>%
      dplyr::filter(CF == "Hot Dry") %>%
      dplyr::select(-CF) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Hot_Dry"),
    by = "Variable"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    wbm_stats %>%
      dplyr::filter(CF == "Warm Wet") %>%
      dplyr::select(-CF) %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Warm_Wet"),
    by = "Variable"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Hot_Dry_pct_change  = (Hot_Dry  - Historical) / Historical * 100,
    Warm_Wet_pct_change = (Warm_Wet - Historical) / Historical * 100
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, Historical, Hot_Dry, Hot_Dry_pct_change, Warm_Wet, Warm_Wet_pct_change)

library(knitr)
save_table(wbm_stats_long, "water_balance_summary")
library(kableExtra)

# Variables measured in gallons (comma-format, 0 decimals)
gal_vars <- c("runoff_gal", "inflow_gal", "inflow_open_months_gal")

wbm_stats_long %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Value columns: gallons get comma formatting, others get 2 decimals
    Historical          = dplyr::if_else(Variable %in% gal_vars,
                            scales::comma(Historical, accuracy = 1),
                            formatC(Historical, format = "f", digits = 2)),
    Hot_Dry             = dplyr::if_else(Variable %in% gal_vars,
                            scales::comma(Hot_Dry, accuracy = 1),
                            formatC(Hot_Dry, format = "f", digits = 2)),
    Warm_Wet            = dplyr::if_else(Variable %in% gal_vars,
                            scales::comma(Warm_Wet, accuracy = 1),
                            formatC(Warm_Wet, format = "f", digits = 2)),
    # Percent change columns: 1 decimal + % sign
    Hot_Dry_pct_change  = paste0(formatC(Hot_Dry_pct_change,  format = "f", digits = 1), "%"),
    Warm_Wet_pct_change = paste0(formatC(Warm_Wet_pct_change, format = "f", digits = 1), "%"),
    # Readable variable names
    Variable = dplyr::recode(Variable,
      tmean_F                = "Mean Temp (°F)",
      precip_in              = "Precipitation (in)",
      rain_in                = "Rain (in)",
      snow_in                = "Snow (in)",
      melt_in                = "Snowmelt (in)",
      aet_in                 = "AET (in)",
      pet_in                 = "PET (in)",
      runoff_in              = "Runoff (in)",
      runoff_gal             = "Runoff (gal)",
      inflow_gal             = "Inflow (gal)",
      inflow_open_months_gal = "Operating Season Inflow (gal)"
    )
  ) %>%
  kable(
    col.names = c("Variable", "Historical", "Hot Dry", "% Change", "Warm Wet", "% Change"),
    align     = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    caption   = "Mean annual water budget components: historical baseline (1980–2012) vs. mid-century futures (2035–2064)"
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
```

Now, we develop a logistic visitation growth model to project future demand, accounting for population growth with an assumed carrying capacity.

```{r logistic_vis_model}
# --- 1. Define Carrying Capacity Bounds ---
K_limit_mid  <- max(visitors_an$LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.5
K_limit_high <- K_limit_mid * 1.2
K_limit_low  <- K_limit_mid * 0.8

# Logistic growth model: K / (1 + exp(-r * (year - t0)))
logistic_mod <- function(K_limit, r, t0, year) {
  K_limit / (1 + exp(-r * (year - t0)))
}

# Fit logistic model via nonlinear least squares for a given K
fit_vis_logistic <- function(K_limit, df) {
  nls(
    LoganVisitors ~ logistic_mod(K_limit, r, t0, year),
    data  = df,
    start = list(r = 0.05, t0 = 2010)
  )
}

# --- 2. Fit Models for Low, Mid, and High Capacity Bounds ---
vis_logistic_low  <- fit_vis_logistic(K_limit_low,  visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020))
vis_logistic_mid  <- fit_vis_logistic(K_limit_mid,  visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020))
vis_logistic_high <- fit_vis_logistic(K_limit_high, visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020))

# --- 3. Predict to 2100 ---
future_years <- data.frame(year = 1980:2100) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pred_vis_low  = predict(vis_logistic_low,  newdata = .),
    pred_vis_mid  = predict(vis_logistic_mid,  newdata = .),
    pred_vis_high = predict(vis_logistic_high, newdata = .)
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = visitors_an, aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors, color = "Obs.")) +
  geom_ribbon(data = future_years,
              aes(x = year, ymin = pred_vis_low, ymax = pred_vis_high), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = future_years, aes(x = year, y = pred_vis_mid, color = "mod")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = K_limit_mid, linetype = "dashed") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Total Visitors", title = "Logistic Visitor Growth Model") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("black", "red"))
```

```{r annual_vis_gam}
# --- 1. Prepare Annual Model Dataset ---
vis_mod_dat <- visitors_an %>%
  left_join(wbm_annual %>% dplyr::filter(year < 2026), by = "year") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pop          = logistic_mod(K_limit_mid,
                                coef(vis_logistic_mid)["r"],
                                coef(vis_logistic_mid)["t0"],
                                year),
    tmean_F_prev = dplyr::lag(tmean_F, 1)
  )

# --- 2. Fit Annual GAM ---
vis_mod <- mgcv::gam(
  LoganVisitors ~ tmean_F + snowpack_in_wbm + pop,
  data = vis_mod_dat
)

# --- 3. Predictions and Residuals ---
vis_mod_dat <- vis_mod_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(year > 1997) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pred_vis          = pmax(0, predict(vis_mod, newdata = .)),
    pred_vis_residual = LoganVisitors - pred_vis
  )

r2_val <- round(summary(vis_mod)$r.sq, 2)
p_val  <- format.pval(mean(summary(vis_mod)$p.pv), digits = 2, eps = 0.001)

# --- 4. Performance Visualization ---
annual_vis_mod_plot <- ggarrange(
  # Panel A: Time Series
  ggplot(vis_mod_dat) +
    geom_line(aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors, color = "Observed"), size = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(x = year, y = pred_vis,      color = "Modeled"),  size = 1) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position        = c(0.85, 0.25),   # x, y in [0,1] plot coordinates
      legend.background      = element_rect(fill = alpha("white", 0.7), color = NA),
      legend.key             = element_blank()
    ) +
    annotate("text",
             label = as.character(as.expression(bquote(R^2 == .(r2_val) ~~~ p < .(p_val)))),
             parse = TRUE, x = -Inf, y = Inf, hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
             size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Annual Visitors", title = "Annual Model Performance") +
    scale_color_manual("", values = c("Modeled" = "tomato", "Observed" = "black")),

  # Panel B: Residuals
  ggplot(vis_mod_dat, aes(x = year, y = pred_vis_residual)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_line() + geom_point() +
    labs(y = "Residual (# visitors)", x = "Year", title = "Annual Residuals") +
    theme_bw(),

  # Panel C: 1:1 Accuracy
  ggplot(vis_mod_dat, aes(x = LoganVisitors, y = pred_vis)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dotted", size = 1) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(
      min(vis_mod_dat$LoganVisitors, vis_mod_dat$pred_vis),
      max(vis_mod_dat$LoganVisitors, vis_mod_dat$pred_vis)
    )) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(
      min(vis_mod_dat$LoganVisitors, vis_mod_dat$pred_vis),
      max(vis_mod_dat$LoganVisitors, vis_mod_dat$pred_vis)
    )) +
    labs(x = "Observed Annual Visitors", y = "Modeled Annual Visitors",
         title = "1:1 Accuracy"),

  ncol = 1, align = "hv"
)

ggsave(plot     = annual_vis_mod_plot,
       filename = "data/park/GLAC/Figs/Annual_vis_mod.jpg",
       dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 4.5)
```

```{r proj_vis}
# --- 1. Project Annual Visitation Using GAM + Logistic Population ---
vis_clim <- wbm_annual %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pop = logistic_mod(K_limit_mid,
                       coef(vis_logistic_mid)["r"],
                       coef(vis_logistic_mid)["t0"],
                       year)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(year, pop, tmean_F, GCM, CF, snowpack_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {
    preds <- predict(vis_mod, newdata = .x, se.fit = TRUE)
    .x %>% mutate(vis_pred    = as.numeric(preds$fit),
                  vis_pred_SE = as.numeric(preds$se.fit))
  }) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    vis_pred_low  = vis_pred - vis_pred_SE * 1.96,
    vis_pred_high = vis_pred + vis_pred_SE * 1.96
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(
    vis_yearly_max  = max(vis_pred_high),
    vis_yearly_min  = min(vis_pred_low),
    vis_yearly_mean = mean(c(vis_pred_high, vis_pred_low), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# --- 2. Fit Smooth Logistic Curves to Projected Bounds ---
# Because GAM predictions vary year-to-year with temperature, we fit smooth
# logistic envelopes for cleaner reporting figures.
fit_smooth_logistic <- function(y_var, df, K) {
  nls(y_var ~ logistic_mod(K, r, t0, year),
      data  = df,
      start = list(r = 0.05, t0 = 2050))
}

log_mod_proj <- fit_smooth_logistic(vis_clim$vis_yearly_mean, vis_clim, max(vis_clim$vis_yearly_mean))
log_mod_high <- fit_smooth_logistic(vis_clim$vis_yearly_max,  vis_clim, max(vis_clim$vis_yearly_max))
log_mod_low  <- fit_smooth_logistic(vis_clim$vis_yearly_min,  vis_clim, max(vis_clim$vis_yearly_min))

vis_clim <- vis_clim %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    vis_smooth_mid  = as.numeric(predict(log_mod_proj, newdata = .)),
    vis_smooth_high = as.numeric(predict(log_mod_high, newdata = .)),
    vis_smooth_low  = as.numeric(predict(log_mod_low,  newdata = .))
  ) %>%
  left_join(visitors_an %>% dplyr::select(year, LoganVisitors), by = "year")

# --- 3. Monthly Visitation Projections ---
proj_vis_sum <- vis_clim %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(in_fut(year)) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_vis = mean(vis_smooth_mid),
    max_vis  = max(vis_smooth_high),
    min_vis  = min(vis_smooth_low)
  )

# Add future monthly estimates to proportion table
monthly_visitor_proportions <- monthly_visitor_proportions %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    fut_min_vis  = proj_vis_sum$min_vis  * fraction,
    fut_max_vis  = proj_vis_sum$max_vis  * fraction,
    fut_mean_vis = proj_vis_sum$mean_vis * fraction
  )

# Expand to full monthly time series (historical = observed; future = smoothed projection)
monthly_visitors <- vis_clim %>%
  full_join(
    data.frame(ym = seq.Date(as.Date("1979-01-01"), as.Date("2099-12-01"), by = "month")) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)),
    by = "year"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    vis_smooth_mid  = mean(vis_smooth_mid,  na.rm = TRUE),
    vis_smooth_low  = min(vis_smooth_low,   na.rm = TRUE),
    vis_smooth_high = max(vis_smooth_high,  na.rm = TRUE),
    LoganVisitors   = mean(LoganVisitors,   na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = month(ym), year = year(ym)) %>%
  left_join(monthly_visitor_proportions %>% dplyr::select(month, fraction), by = "month") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    monthly_vis      = ifelse(year < 2025, fraction * LoganVisitors,   fraction * vis_smooth_mid),
    monthly_vis_high = ifelse(year < 2025, fraction * LoganVisitors,   fraction * vis_smooth_high),
    monthly_vis_low  = ifelse(year < 2025, fraction * LoganVisitors,   fraction * vis_smooth_low)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, monthly_vis_low, monthly_vis_high, monthly_vis)
```

#### - Water use

We estimate water use based on visitation with low, mid, and high per-visitor use rates from the observed July–August record.

```{r water_use}
# Per-visitor water demand (gallons/visitor): minimum, mean, and maximum of the
# observed July–August rates (chunk `use_per_visitor_summary`)
low_use_per_visitor  <- round(obs_use_per_visitor$min_use_pv,  2)
mid_use_per_visitor  <- round(obs_use_per_visitor$mean_use_pv, 2)
high_use_per_visitor <- round(obs_use_per_visitor$max_use_pv,  2)

# --- Monthly Use Estimates ---
monthly_use <- monthly_visitors %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(ym) > 1997) %>%
  arrange(ym) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = month(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    monthly_use_low  = monthly_vis_low  * low_use_per_visitor,
    monthly_use_mid  = monthly_vis      * mid_use_per_visitor,
    monthly_use_high = monthly_vis_high * high_use_per_visitor
  ) %>%
  # Apply seasonal mask: zero use in winter/early spring, partial use at shoulder seasons
  dplyr::mutate(across(
    c(monthly_use_low, monthly_use_high, monthly_use_mid),
    ~ case_when(
      month %in% c(10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) ~ 0,
      month %in% c(9)                           ~ . * 0.25,
      month %in% c(6)                           ~ . * 0.75,
      month %in% c(7, 8)                        ~ .
    )
  )) %>%
  left_join(logan_sd_monthly, by = "ym")

# Annual use totals
annual_use <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mid_use   = sum(monthly_use_mid,  na.rm = TRUE),
    low_use   = sum(monthly_use_low,  na.rm = TRUE),
    high_use  = sum(monthly_use_high, na.rm = TRUE),
    actual_use = sum(use_gal,         na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    c_group    = ifelse(year <= 2025, "Historical", "Projected"),
    actual_use = ifelse(actual_use == 0, NA, actual_use)
  )

# Monthly use proportions table (for reference and supply:demand analysis)
# Values are in gallons
monthly_use_proportions <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year != 2020) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(month) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mid_use_obs  = mean(use_gal,                                   na.rm = TRUE),
    mid_use_hist = mean(monthly_use_mid[year < 2025],              na.rm = TRUE),
    mid_use_fut  = mean(monthly_use_mid[in_fut(year)]),
    low_use_hist = mean(monthly_use_low[year < 2025],              na.rm = TRUE),
    low_use_fut  = mean(monthly_use_low[in_fut(year)]),
    high_use_hist = mean(monthly_use_high[year < 2025],            na.rm = TRUE),
    high_use_fut  = mean(monthly_use_high[in_fut(year)])
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    month_date = as_date(paste0("2000-", month, "-01")),
    fraction   = mid_use_hist / sum(mid_use_hist)
  )

# Some use stats for the report

use_2025 <- annual_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(year == 2025)

use_2050 <- annual_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(year == 2050)

monthly_use_2025 <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(month(ym) == 7,
                year(ym) == 2025)

monthly_use_2050 <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::filter(month(ym) == 7,
                year(ym) == 2050)

print(paste0("2050 use ranges from ", floor(use_2050$low_use), 
             " to ", floor(use_2050$high_use), " gallons with a mean of ",
             floor(use_2050$mid_use), " gallons representing a ",
      floor(100* (use_2050$mid_use - use_2025$actual_use)/use_2025$actual_use), 
      "% increase from observed 2025 use of ", use_2025$actual_use, "."))

print(paste0("July use increases from the 2025 rate of ", floor(monthly_use_2025$use_gal), " gallons to ", floor(monthly_use_2050$monthly_use_mid), 
      " gallons in 2050, an increase of ", 
      floor(100* (monthly_use_2050$monthly_use_mid - monthly_use_2025$use_gal)/monthly_use_2025$use_gal), "%."))



```

```{r monthly_supply_demand}
# Monthly supply and demand dataset
monthly_sd <- wbm_monthly %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, inflow_gal, inflow_gal_low, inflow_gal_high) %>%
  left_join(monthly_use %>%
              dplyr::select(ym, monthly_use_low, monthly_use_mid, monthly_use_high, use_gal),
            by = "ym")

# Monthly demand in long format (for supply:demand figure)
monthly_use_long <- monthly_use_proportions %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = matches("(mid|low|high)_use_(fut|hist)"),
    names_to  = "use_cat",
    values_to = "use_cf"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_date = case_when(
      grepl("hist", use_cat) ~ month_date - years(4),
      TRUE                   ~ month_date + years(50)
    ),
    new_group  = case_when(
      grepl("low",  use_cat) ~ "low_use",
      grepl("high", use_cat) ~ "high_use",
      TRUE                   ~ "mid_use"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(month_date, new_group, use_cf) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = new_group, values_from = use_cf)

# --- Demand:Supply Ratio Analysis ---
DS_df <- wbm_annual %>%
  select(year, CF, inflow_gal, inflow_open_months_gal, runoff_cf) %>%
  left_join(annual_use, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(
    DS          = mid_use  / inflow_open_months_gal,
    DS_stress   = high_use / inflow_open_months_gal,
    DS_over_pt2 = if_else(DS >= 0.2, 1, 0),
    DS_over_1   = if_else(DS >= 1,   1, 0)
  )

DS_stats <- DS_df %>%
  filter(in_window(year)) %>%
  group_by(CF) %>%
  summarize(
    n                       = n(),
    high_stress_years       = 100 * sum(DS_over_pt2) / n,
    inadequate_supply_years = 100 * sum(DS_over_1)   / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(DS_stats)
```
